items.claim: The row rejects an internal seam at the setumah the mark layer places on MT 22:18 on the ground that no formula device stands there, and that ground is false on the witness and on the device lists. The messenger formula stands at MT 22:19, the verse immediately after that mark, as “לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה”, and MT 22:19 is a member of the 122-verse messenger list; the divine address to the prophet stands at MT 22:18 itself and that verse is a member of the 93-verse address list. Both are quoted in the row's own Hebrew tag list, so the row contradicts its own evidence. The span and the boundaries are nevertheless right: MT 22:17 is wholly the strict onset formula, MT 22:22 is quoted whole and closes on a second-person-plural recognition pattern that the row correctly reports as outside the strict lists, and the mark layer records a petuchah at MT 22:22. items.both_sides: At the mark on MT 22:18: behind it stands only the address to the prophet, one verse into a unit whose onset formula is MT 22:17, with no close-grade refrain anywhere between; ahead of it MT 22:19 brings the messenger formula, which in this book opens a speech inside a unit and becomes a sub-onset only when the addressee changes or a close precedes it, and neither holds here. items.claim: Two Masoretic facts on the seam this row rejects are missing from it, and together they are the strongest evidence against the row's own confidence. First, a setumah stands at MT 24:24: the row cites that verse five times, as the sign naming, as a recognition-pattern close and as paragraph-final, and never names the mark or its kind, so a setumah is reported only by allusion and never distinguished from a petuchah. Second, the row's ground for refusing a seam at MT 24:24/24:25 enumerates the devices that do not open MT 24:25 and omits the one that does: MT 24:25 opens “וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם”, the sub-onset that begins a fresh command without an onset formula, and the verse is a member of the 93-verse divine-address list. So the configuration at MT 24:24/24:25 is exactly the shape this corpus treats as a live seam candidate, a refrain-grade close with a mark followed by that sub-onset. The row's span can stand, but its confidence cannot: the same configuration one chapter earlier, a setumah behind at MT 23:35 with a fresh address at MT 23:36, is held at medium in this very part, and the same standard applied here yields medium. Separately, and as the triage asks: the petuchah at MT 24:14 is not disclosed by this row either, which cites that verse for its two closing formulae only; it corroborates the onset, so it changes nothing but the disclosure. The row's positive facts are all true: MT 24:15 is quoted whole and belongs to both the 39-verse strict and 41-verse any-form counts, MT 24:27 is quoted whole and is chapter 24's only member of the 28-verse strict recognition list with a setumah recorded on it, the sign naming at MT 24:24 is an exact prefix, the two strokes at MT 24:17 and MT 24:21 are in the paseq layer, and no variant site falls inside MT 24:15-27.
items.both_sides: For a seam at MT 24:25: MT 24:24 ends on a second-person-plural recognition pattern with the Lord-YHWH divine-name variant and the mark layer records a setumah on it; MT 24:25 opens “וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם”, the sub-onset that starts a fresh command with no onset formula behind it, and the subject turns from the enacted sign to the fugitive's arrival and the opening of the prophet's mouth. Against a seam: the sign word “לְמוֹפֵ֔ת” at MT 24:24 recurs as “וְהָיִ֤יתָ” at MT 24:27, binding the two ends of the span together; MT 24:27 carries the strict third-person recognition formula and a setumah that close the whole collection; and no dated, strict-onset or messenger device opens MT 24:25, so the sub-onset alone sits below hard-seam grade and a three-verse tail would fall under the granularity target. I therefore keep the span and move the confidence, rather than cutting.
